category_title: Students exhibiting physical resistance to classroom routines
minimal_context: Stephen is in the classroom during the morning routine and is expected to stand for the Pledge of Allegiance.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for the morning routine. Please stand up for the Pledge of Allegiance.

STUDENT: (Remains seated in his chair and does not stand for the Pledge of Allegiance.)

TUTOR: You need to stand up now. (Walks up to him and raises him from the chair)

STUDENT: (Starts moving, trying to get away from her.)

TUTOR: (Holds him strongly) If you continue with this behavior, you won't have computer.

STUDENT: (Continues moving and physically resisting, trying to get away from her hold.)

options.A: Support Stephen's needs through shared power by compromising, negotiating situations, or sharing decisions instead of trying to impose control over his behavior for every routine.
options.B: Operate a 'level method' (A-E) where staff assign Stephen a level based on his previous week's behavior during the morning routine and other activities.
options.C: Provide a clear beginning and end for each task during the morning routine and throughout the rest of the daily classroom schedule.
options.D: Review Stephen's Thumbs Up sheet with him and have him count all of the thumbs up and thumbs down that are circled for the morning routine.
